title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.title: How you fall
chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

chapters.title: Your flirting style
chapters.teaser: What you think you're doing, what they think you're doing, and the one move that lands.

chapters.title: Your attachment pattern
chapters.teaser: Clingy, cool, steady or somewhere in between. How you hold on when you care.

chapters.teaser: The exact thing that sets you off, and what you do instead of saying it.

text.how-you-fall: You fall like a mountain moves: very slowly, and then it's permanent. Mu is the big hill, the boulder, the thing you can lean against without checking. You don't do impulsive crushes. You observe someone for a long time, quietly gathering evidence that they're trustworthy, consistent and worth the effort of letting in. By the time you show interest, you've basically already decided. That means rejection hits harder than you'd ever show. On the bright side, when you choose someone, they feel deeply safe. You become their shelter: the person who drives over in the rain, fixes the shelf, remembers the doctor appointment. The risk is that you're so focused on being solid that your partner might not realize you're also falling, because mountains don't exactly blush.
text.flirting: You flirt by being useful, and you may not even call it flirting. Carrying their bags, making sure they got home, showing up with snacks because they mentioned they skipped lunch. It's steady, practical care, and the people who notice it melt. The people who don't might wonder if you're interested at all, because you rarely say the soft thing out loud. Your humour helps a lot here. Dry, understated jokes are your secret weapon, and when you let them out, people get a glimpse of the warm landscape behind the cliff face. Try one small step past comfort: tell them you like them, plainly. You don't need poetry. "I like spending time with you" from a mountain sounds like a whole sonnet.
text.attachment: Your pattern looks secure and sometimes leans avoidant. You're reliable and calm, the opposite of dramatic, and you rarely panic about where a relationship stands. But emotional conversations can make you go quiet and still, like a hill waiting out a storm. You'd rather fix a problem than talk about how it feels, and when a partner wants to process, you might reach for solutions or simply shut down until it passes. That's not coldness. It's how you protect a very big, very loyal heart. Your growth edge is staying present in the feelings part. Sit in the conversation without fixing it. Say "that sounds hard" and mean it. You'll be surprised how much closer people feel when the mountain just listens.
text.jealousy: You rarely get jealous, and when you do, it looks like nothing. That's the problem. You don't sulk or accuse. You just become a little more distant, a little more silent, and quietly start reconsidering how much you trust this person. Your trigger is inconsistency. If someone says one thing and does another, flirts openly when they promised they wouldn't, or hides something small, your entire internal foundation shifts. You don't care much about rivals. You care about reliability. Because you don't express it, the other person might not realize there's anything wrong until you've already half withdrawn. Say it while it's still small. "I noticed this and it bothered me." Mountains erode slowly. It's better to repair one crack than rebuild the whole slope.
text.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you're stubborn to the point of geology. Once you've decided how something should go, you stop listening, and your partner feels like they're arguing with a wall. A very kind, very supportive wall, but a wall. Second flag: you mistake stability for romance. You can stay comfortable in a relationship that stopped growing years ago because it's familiar and safe. "Nothing's wrong" is not the same as "this is good." Third: you shut down instead of fighting. The silent treatment isn't punishment for you, it's processing, but to your partner it feels like being frozen out. You're allowed to need time. Just say "I need an hour, then let's talk" instead of disappearing into rock.
text.what-you-need: You need trust, and you need it earned. A partner who is consistent, keeps small promises, and doesn't play games, because you have zero patience for mind tricks. You need someone who appreciates quiet loyalty and doesn't need constant performance of affection to feel loved. Gentle encouragement helps you too: someone who invites you to try new things without pushing, who brings a little colour and spontaneity to your steady life. And you need someone who understands that your love shows up as action. When you cook for them or sort out their car, that's a declaration. The best person for you feels like a clear day on a mountain. Calm, open, and worth staying for.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, you love like a mountain. Solid, protective, the safest place anyone's ever stood.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also about as emotionally chatty as a mountain.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your love is in actions! You drive over in the rain.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And when they want to talk about feelings, you suggest fixing the shelf.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Try saying "I like you" out loud. From you it sounds like poetry.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Comfortable is not the same as happy. Check which one you're in.

spring.intro: Spring is Wood's season, and Wood controls Earth, so a spring-born Mu Earth is a mountain with roots pushing through every crack. You grew up feeling pulled by other people's growth, and in love you are often the steady one everyone leans on. You fall slowly and seriously, and you can mistake being needed for being loved. Partners who are restless or ambitious find you irresistible, because you hold still while they flourish. The pressure of the season makes you sturdy, not stiff. What strengthens you is Fire, your resource: warmth, praise, someone who notices your effort without being told. Being the mountain is lovely. Being admired as one is better.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Mu, 'they rely on me' and 'they love me' are two separate sentences. Check which.

summer.intro: Summer is Fire's season, and Fire feeds Earth, so a summer-born Mu Earth is a sun-warmed mountain: solid, generous and difficult to move. You love with full confidence. Once you have chosen someone, you consider the matter settled, which is wonderful for stability and a little alarming for spontaneity. With so much support behind you, your blind spot is assuming your way is the sensible way. You can turn down every new idea by calmly listing reasons, and the person you love stops suggesting things. Metal, the element you produce, is your growth edge: expressing what you feel, not just what you think. Say 'I missed you' out loud. Mountains can echo.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Mu, you're the safest place they know. Now say one soft thing out loud today.

autumn.intro: Autumn is Metal's season, and Earth produces Metal, so an autumn-born Mu Earth spends itself making something valuable. You are the mountain full of ore: you give gifts, solutions and practical care, and you rarely ask for anything in return. In love, that looks like quiet acts of service. You will drive across town at midnight but struggle to say what is bothering you. Over time, giving so much drains the reserves, and you can become heavy or withdrawn without explaining why. Fire, your resource, is how you refill: being appreciated, being made a fuss of, a partner who notices when you are worn out before you announce it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Mu, you fixed their shelf, their car and their CV. Did anyone ask how you are?

winter.intro: Winter is Water's season, and Earth controls Water, so a winter-born Mu Earth is a frozen mountain holding back a lake. You have a lot of feeling stored up and a strong instinct to manage it. In love you are reliable and patient, but you can be slow to warm, and your partner might wonder what is happening beneath the snow. You see love as responsibility: keeping things stable, avoiding drama, looking after the practical side. The cold season makes Fire precious for you. Laughter, affection, a partner who drags you to a lively dinner. Warmth is not a distraction from commitment. For a winter mountain, it is the thing that lets spring come.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Mu, you hold so much in. Let one warm person past the snowline.

strength.strong: A strong Mu Earth is a mountain that does not move for anyone. With plenty of Earth and Fire in your chart, you are steady, protective and very sure of what is sensible. In love you give enormous security, but you can also become immovable. Your blind spot is overpowering through stubbornness: refusing new plans, settling arguments by simply not budging, assuming your partner will adjust. They usually do, until one day they stop. Practise saying 'let's try it your way' and actually meaning it. A mountain that lets a path through is still a mountain. It is just easier to love.
strength.weak: A weak Mu Earth is a hill being leaned on from every side. With little Earth or Fire support, you still want to be the reliable one, so you carry partners through crises you cannot really afford. You may become the emergency contact, the fixer, the person who never needs anything. Your blind spot is over-giving until you feel empty and heavy at once. Then you go quiet and nobody knows why. Ask for help before you reach that point. Let your partner be the solid ground for a week. Being held is not weakness. It is what lets mountains stay standing.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood in your chart turns love into a growth plan. You want things to move forward, define the relationship, make progress, and slow phases make you restless. You can also be stubborn in arguments, holding your position like a tree in wind. In love this looks like big intentions and a little impatience. Balance it with Metal energy: clear agreements, pruning what isn't working, and accepting that some things are already finished growing. Not every relationship needs to become a forest. Some are perfect as a single, steady tree.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means beginnings are your hard part. You might wait for the other person to make the first move, define things, or suggest the next step, and you can stay in a comfortable but stuck situation for too long. Your love is real, it just doesn't push. Balance it by practising small starts: suggest the date, send the first text, say what you hope for out loud. Green things help as reminders, a plant by your bed, a green phone case. Love grows when someone plants it. Sometimes that someone is you.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your love bright, fast and a little combustible. You fall hard, flirt boldly and feel everything at full volume. The highs are glorious. The lows, when attention drops, feel like the lights went out. You can also lose interest once the excitement settles. Balance it with Water energy: slowing down, letting quiet evenings count, and sitting with feelings before reacting. Ask yourself if you love the person or the thrill. The best flame for you burns steady, not just bright.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means passion and visibility don't come easily in love. You might care deeply but struggle to show it, hold back affection until you're sure, or feel awkward with romantic gestures. People can mistake your reserve for disinterest. Balance it by letting warmth out in small, brave doses: a compliment, a hug that lasts a second longer, a little playfulness. Warm colours and sunlight help you feel more expressive. You don't need fireworks. You just need people to see that the light is on.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth makes you a steady, devoted partner who can get a little stuck. You value security, routine and loyalty, and you might stay in familiar patterns even when they've stopped making you happy. Change feels risky. You may also over-care, taking on your partner's problems as your own. Balance it with Wood energy: try something new together, plan an adventure, let the relationship grow in surprising directions. Safe is wonderful. Safe and alive is even better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means love can feel unsteady. You might worry about where things stand, struggle to settle into commitment, or jump between highs and lows. You can also find it hard to trust that someone will stay. Balance it by building small, reliable rituals: a weekly date, a regular call, a shared routine. Choose partners who are consistent rather than exciting. Earth tones and home-cooked meals help you feel grounded. Stability isn't boring. For you, it's what lets love feel safe enough to enjoy.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives you strong standards and very clear boundaries in love. You know what you want and what you won't tolerate, which is healthy, until it becomes rigid. You can be critical, quick to judge, or end things abruptly when disappointed. Balance it with Fire energy: warmth, forgiveness, play. Let small mistakes be small. Say the kind thing before the honest thing. Strong boundaries keep you safe. Soft edges let people actually come close enough to love you.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are your hard part in love. You might say yes when you mean no, stay too long, or let people treat you less well than you deserve because you don't want conflict. Your heart is open, sometimes too open. Balance it by practising clear, simple limits: "I'm not okay with that," without a long explanation. Decluttering and white or silver accents can help you feel sharper. Boundaries aren't walls. They're the frame that makes the picture of your love clear.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water makes your love deep, intuitive and sometimes overwhelming. You feel everything, read every mood and can get lost in emotional currents or imagined stories. You may also avoid commitment, drifting rather than choosing. Balance it with Earth energy: grounding conversations, practical plans, partners who are steady and clear. Write down what actually happened before reacting to what you feel happened. Your depth is beautiful. It just needs a shore so you don't get swept away.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means emotional depth and rest don't come easily in love. You might stay busy, keep conversations practical, or struggle to sit with vulnerable feelings, yours or your partner's. Love can feel like a to-do list. Balance it with slow, quiet moments: late talks, journaling, listening without fixing. Navy and black, water by your bed, and slow evenings help you soften. You don't need to drown in feelings. Just let yourself wade in a little deeper.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you want it defined, labelled and growing by Thursday. Breathe.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your hope is beautiful. Let it grow at the speed of a real person.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: you fall hard, fast and loudly. Then the second act bores you.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is a gift. Let it simmer a while. Slow love tastes better.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: staying somewhere stale because leaving takes effort isn't loyalty. It's inertia.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Make sure it's going somewhere that still feeds you.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: your dating checklist has forty points. Nobody passes. Including you.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Standards protect you. Leave one door open for someone surprising.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: you wrote a whole love story in your head. They've read none of it.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is gorgeous. Share a little of it with the real person.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Love won't start itself. Send the first text. Plant something.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Waiting for them to make the move isn't patience. It's hiding behind a nice word.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? Your love is real, it just whispers. Let someone hear it.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: A compliment you only think doesn't count. Say it, then survive the blushing.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? You love brightly but drift. A small weekly ritual keeps you anchored.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Three crushes, zero follow-through. Pick one and show up twice in a row.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? Your kindness needs a boundary. A no keeps your yes worth something.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Three cancellations and a fourth chance isn't generosity. It's a pattern you're funding.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? You act before you feel. Pause and ask what you actually want.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Over someone in a weekend isn't healing. It's skipping the chapter. Read it.
